key_insight: Protocol stages in quantum identity authentication can be inferred from non-invasive optical side channels, threatening the security of the entire quantum authentication flow.
engineering_relevance: Quantum communication systems need protections against side-channel leakage, not just protocol-level MitM defenses, to prevent attackers from identifying and bypassing authentication qubits.
method: Used a beam splitter to tap side-channel data without disturbing the quantum state
Collected photon arrival timing and optical power with a single-photon detector and power meter
Trained machine-learning classifiers on engineered timing and intensity features to identify protocol stages
evidence_signal: Across two sampling settings, the models achieved 98% accuracy (F1 97%) at 30% sampling and 96% accuracy (F1 94%) at 10% sampling.
watch_item: The study uses a controlled testbed, so real deployment conditions, device variability, and additional noise sources may reduce inference performance.
paper_title: Experimental Side Channel Analysis of Protocol Stages in Quantum Identity Authentication
